suites.description: 1D mission of 1500 mm in 16 ticks at 250 mm per tick; the clean base has no violation.
2D mission (250 mm east, 2000 mm north) in 12 ticks at 500 mm per tick; separates the two axis policies.

Known-faulty M3 base: GPS dropout at ticks 4 to 10 and a 3-tick delayed command, with fallback_after_ticks 2 already set. The 5000 mm mission cannot finish in 14 ticks, so it stresses fallback, not progress.

baseline.rationale: Canonical M4 controller: dominant-axis heading, watchdog after 3 low-confidence ticks, recovery after 2, confidence gate 500 permille, scenario stride.

candidates.rationale: Watchdog latency must not exceed the 2-tick fallback_response deadline. Assumes localization loss is visible within one tick, so an earlier stop costs only availability under short transient dropouts.

Halving the commanded displacement per tick halves the distance covered by a delayed, continued or noise-misdirected command, so overshoot and late motion shrink. Cost: the mission needs twice as many ticks and can run out of horizon.

Paralysis control. Act only on high-confidence fixes. Confidence decays with sample age, so 800 accepts only same-tick data and any delay makes the vehicle hold. The threshold also defines the localization_unreliable trigger, so this candidate changes the oracle. The paired completion gate must reject it.

watchdog_2 with recovery after one reliable tick. A 2-tick watchdog with 2-tick recovery can stay in fallback under alternating dropouts (U,U,R,U,U,R); faster recovery should keep the timing fix without that availability loss, at the risk of leaving fallback on a single good sample.
Known-weaker policy from M4 (axis order ignores the larger error). Included as a negative control: the regression engine must flag it.
